lines: [VERIFIED] STAT — US Department of Housing and Urban Development: "Past thirty percent of income spent on housing, a household counts as cost-burde" — HUD states that housing cost burden means monthly housing costs exceeding 30% of monthly income, and HUD-aligned sources repeat the same threshold[1][6].

[VERIFIED] EVENT — US Department of Housing and Urban Development: "HUD adopted the thirty percent figure in 1981" — HUD’s 1985–2005 trends paper says the 30-percent standard “probably originates” in federally assisted housing rules and that “in 1981, Congress changed the minimum payment to 30 percent of income,” which supports the cla

[UNVERIFIABLE] EVENT — (unnamed): "Earlier public-housing programmes had used twenty-five percent" — The retrieved sources discuss public-housing policy but do not clearly establish that “earlier public-housing programmes had used twenty-five percent,” so the claim could not be confirmed or contradicted from the availab

[CONTRADICTED] EVENT — Senator Edward Brooke: "The thirty percent threshold is traced to a 1969 amendment by Senator Edward Bro" — The sources found say Senator Edward Brooke’s 1969 amendment set public-housing rent at 25%, and that the 30% threshold was raised later in 1981, so tracing the 30% threshold directly to the 1969 amendment is inaccurate[

[UNVERIFIABLE] STAT — NYU Furman Center: "Median household income in the community district covering Windsor Terrace and S" — The search results confirm NYU Furman Center has community-profile data for Brooklyn and related districts, but they do not show a source stating that the Windsor Terrace/Sunset Park community district’s median household

[CONTRADICTED] STAT — StreetEasy: "Median asking rent in the area was $2,250 in 2021" — StreetEasy’s 2021 reports show materially different 2021 median asking rent figures, including $2,700 citywide in Q1 2021 and Q4 2021, and $2,699 in Q3 2021, so the claim that the median asking rent in the area was $2,25

[UNVERIFIABLE] STAT — StreetEasy: "Median asking rent in the area was $3,800 five years later" — StreetEasy sources show median asking rent reaching $3,800 in specific NYC contexts and dates, but the exact claim that it was “$3,800 five years later” is not directly confirmed from the available source material[1].

[UNVERIFIABLE] EVENT — (unnamed): "Citi Bike docks arrived in 2021" — A NYC DOT press release from April 7, 2021 says Citi Bike expanded with new stations and “bike docks,” and a December 2021 news report also describes new Citi Bike docking stations arriving in 2021, supporting the claim
